title: Tenali Raman and the Disputed Bullock Cart
summary: Two traveling grain merchants, Shankara and Ramadas, appeared before the royal magistrate of Vijayanagara, both claiming ownership of a sturdy, red wooden bullock cart pulled by...
full_text:
Two traveling grain merchants, Shankara and Ramadas, appeared before the royal magistrate of Vijayanagara, both claiming ownership of a sturdy, red wooden bullock cart pulled by two white Kangayam oxen.
Shankara swore: 'I bought the cart in Bellary two months ago; Ramadas stole it while I was eating at an inn!'
Ramadas yelled: 'A lie! I had the cart built by my village carpenter; it is mine!'

Both men produced receipts from different carpenters, and the magistrate was baffled.
Tenali Raman was invited to resolve the dispute.

Tenali inspected the cart and the two white bullocks.
He said: 'Maharaj, paper receipts can be forged, but the memory of animals cannot be bribed.
Let us take the cart to the Great Crossroads outside the city, where four highways branch off to four different provinces.'

The court retinue rode to the four-way crossroads.
Tenali had both merchants stand in the center of the road, fifty paces away from the cart.
Tenali ordered the driver to step down, loosened the reins completely, and placed them loosely upon the oxen's backs.
Tenali clapped his hands: 'Go home, brothers!'

The two white oxen turned their heads, sniffed the air, and without hesitation, turned down the southern road leading toward Ramadas’s village!
The cart trotted for two miles down the highway, turned into a narrow country lane, entered an open village farmhouse courtyard, and walked straight up to the feeding trough, where two young children ran out shouting:
'Father's cart is home!'

Tenali turned to the King and the assembly:
'An animal knows its own stable, its own trough, and the voices of its master's children!
Nature has delivered the verdict!'

Shankara hung his head in shame, confessing that he had stolen the cart from an inn.
The cart and oxen were restored to honest Ramadas, Shankara was fined thirty silver coins, and the people celebrated Tenali Raman’s reliance on the incorruptible truth of nature.
moral: Animals know their own homes; releasing the reins reveals the true master.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Tenali Raman Tale 148"?
options: Wit and humor triumph over arrogance and power
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?

By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
